completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_fourierTransform_mul_conj
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.7_5 (Parseval's formula): for `f`, `g` absolutely and square integrable,
`∫ F(x) conj(G(x)) dx = ∫ f(t) conj(g(t)) dt`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierConvolution_eq_integral
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.6: for `f`, `g` absolutely and square integrable,
`(f * g)(t) = (2π)^{-1/2} ∫ F(x) G(x) e^{-itx} dx`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_fourierTransform_mul
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.7: for `f`, `g` absolutely and square integrable,
`∫ F(x) G(x) dx = ∫ f(t) g(-t) dt`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_fourierCosTransform_mul
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.13: for `f`, `g` absolutely and square integrable on `[0, ∞)`,
`∫₀^∞ F_c(x) G_c(x) dx = ∫₀^∞ f(t) g(t) dt`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_fourierSinTransform_mul
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.14: for `f`, `g` absolutely and square integrable on `[0, ∞)`,
`∫₀^∞ F_s(x) G_s(x) dx = ∫₀^∞ f(t) g(t) dt`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.differentiableOn_mellin
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.14(iv): if `x^{σ-1} f(x)` is integrable on `(0, ∞)` for all `σ ∈ (a, b)`, then
`𝓜(f)(s)` is analytic in the strip `a < ℜs < b`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integrableOn_stieltjes_integrand
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.14(vi): if `f` is locally integrable on `[0, ∞)` and `f(t) = O(t^{-δ})` as `t → ∞`
with `δ > 0`, then the integral 1.14.47 converges absolutely for every real `s > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.differentiableOn_stieltjesTransform
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.14(vi): if the integral 1.14.47 converges absolutely at one point `s₀ > 0`, then
`𝒮(f)(s)` is analytic in the `s`-plane cut along the negative real axis (Mathlib's
`Complex.slitPlane`). (Absolute convergence makes DLMF's uniform convergence on compact sets
automatic.)

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.iteratedDeriv_stieltjesTransform
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.48: under the hypotheses of `differentiableOn_stieltjesTransform`,
`(dᵐ/dsᵐ) 𝒮(f)(s) = (-1)ᵐ m! ∫₀^∞ f(t)/(s + t)^{m+1} dt` on the cut plane.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.stieltjesTransform_eq_laplace_laplace
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.50: if `f` is locally integrable on `[0, ∞)` and the integral 1.14.47 converges
(absolutely, at `s = 1`), then `𝒮(f)(s) = 𝓛(𝓛(f))(s)` for `ℜs > 0`, where the inner transform
is evaluated at real arguments.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_mul_exp_neg_abs
completed.doc: DLMF Table 1.14.1, row 4: `t e^{-a|t|} ↦ √(2/π) 2iax/(a² + x²)²`, `a > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_abs_mul_exp_neg_abs
completed.doc: DLMF Table 1.14.1, row 5: `|t| e^{-a|t|} ↦ √(2/π) (a² - x²)/(a² + x²)²`, `a > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierCosTransform_gaussian
completed.doc: DLMF Table 1.14.2, row 7: `e^{-at²} ↦ (2a)^{-1/2} e^{-x²/(4a)}`, `ℜa > 0`, principal power.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierSinTransform_mul_gaussian
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.3, row 11: `t e^{-at²} ↦ (2a)^{-3/2} x e^{-x²/(4a)}`, `|ph a| < ½π`
(that is, `ℜa > 0`), principal power.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.mellin_indicator_lt
completed.doc: DLMF Table 1.14.5, row 2: `f = 1` for `x < a`, `0` for `x ≥ a`: `a^s/s`, `a ≥ 0`, `ℜs > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.mellin_log_indicator_lt
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.5, row 3: `ln(a/x)` for `x < a`, `0` for `x ≥ a`: `a^s/s²`, `a ≥ 0`;
valid for `ℜs > 0` (DLMF: `ℜs > 1`).

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.ritt_isBigO
completed.doc:
DLMF §2.1(ii), **Ritt's theorem**: if `f` is analytic in the sector
`𝐒 = {R < |z|, |ph(z e^{-iθ})| < ω}` and `f(z) = O(z^ν)` as `z → ∞` in `𝐒` (`ν` real, so
`|z^ν| = |z|^ν`), then `f'(z) = O(z^{ν-1})` as `z → ∞` in every closed sector
`|ph(z e^{-iθ})| ≤ ω'`, `ω' < ω`, properly interior to `𝐒` with the same vertex.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.ritt_isLittleO
completed.doc: DLMF §2.1(ii): Ritt's theorem with both `O`'s replaced by `o`'s.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.laplace_error_bound
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.3.3 and the bound after it: let `q` be infinitely differentiable on `[0, ∞)` with
`q^{(n)}(0) ≠ 0`, and let `σ` bound `t⁻¹ ln|q^{(n)}(t)/q^{(n)}(0)|` on `(0, ∞)`, that is,
`|q^{(n)}(t)| ≤ |q^{(n)}(0)| e^{σt}` (DLMF's `σₙ` of 2.3.3 is the least such `σ`). Then for
`x > max(0, σ)` the `n`th error term of 2.3.2 is bounded by `|q^{(n)}(0)/(xⁿ(x - σ))|`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_hasGeneralizedAsymptoticExpansion
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.3.4 (finite Fourier integral): if `q` is infinitely differentiable on `[a, b]`, then
`∫ₐᵇ e^{ixt} q(t) dt ∼ e^{iax} ∑ q^{(s)}(a)(i/x)^{s+1} - e^{ibx} ∑ q^{(s)}(b)(i/x)^{s+1}` as
`x → +∞`, a generalized asymptotic expansion with respect to the scale `x^{-s-1}`
(one-sided derivatives at the endpoints).

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_error_bound
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.3.4 with the error bound after 2.3.6: for `n ≥ 1` and `x > 0` the `n`th error term
of 2.3.4 is bounded in absolute value by `x⁻ⁿ 𝒱_{a,b}(q^{(n-1)})`, with the variational operator
2.3.6.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_Ioi_hasGeneralizedAsymptoticExpansion
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.3.5 (infinite Fourier integral): if `q` is infinitely differentiable on `[a, ∞)` and
each integral `∫ₐ^∞ e^{ixt} q^{(s)}(t) dt` converges (as `lim_{T→∞} ∫ₐᵀ`) uniformly for
`x ≥ x₀`, then the improper integral `I(x) = ∫ₐ^∞ e^{ixt} q(t) dt` satisfies
`I(x) ∼ e^{iax} ∑ q^{(s)}(a)(i/x)^{s+1}` as `x → +∞` (generalized expansion, scale `x^{-s-1}`),
and for `n ≥ 1`, `x ≥ max(x₀, 0)`, `x > 0`, the `n`th error term is at most
`x⁻ⁿ ∫ₐ^∞ |q^{(n)}(t)| dt` (`= x⁻ⁿ 𝒱_{a,∞}(q^{(n-1)})`) when that integral is finite.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.harmonic_remainder_bound
completed.doc:
DLMF §2.10(i) (remainder of 2.10.8): after the terms `s < m` of `∑ B_{2s}/(2s) n^{-2s}`
(`m ≥ 1`), the remainder is bounded in absolute value by the first neglected term
`-B_{2m}/(2m) n^{-2m}` and has the same sign, for every `n ≥ 1`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.oscillatorySum_isBigO_trivial
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.10.12 (orders): `∑_{j=1}^{n-1} j^α = O(1)`, `O(ln n)` or `O(n^{α+1})` according as
`α < -1`, `α = -1` or `α > -1`; hence the same bounds for `S(α, β, n)`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.rpow_sub_rpow_succ
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.10.15: for every real `α` there is `C` with
`|j^α - (j+1)^α + α j^{α-1}| ≤ C |α(α-1)| j^{α-2}` for all integers `j ≥ 1`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.inv_sqrt_two_pi_mul_two
newHelpers.doc: The two-sided Fourier normalization turns a factor of `2` into `sqrt(2/π)`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_conj_neg
newHelpers.doc: Conjugating and reflecting a function conjugates its Fourier transform.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_comp_sub
newHelpers.doc: Translating a function multiplies its Fourier transform by the corresponding phase.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integrable_evenExtension
newHelpers.doc: The even extension of a half-line function belongs to `L¹`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.memLp_oddExtension
newHelpers.doc:
An extension odd away from zero belongs to the same `Lᵖ` space. The value at zero
is irrelevant for Lebesgue measure.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_evenExtension
newHelpers.doc: The Fourier transform of an even extension is the cosine transform.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierTransform_oddExtension
newHelpers.doc: The Fourier transform of an extension odd away from zero is `i` times the sine transform.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierCosTransform_abs
newHelpers.doc: A cosine transform is even in its frequency.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierSinTransform_mul_abs
newHelpers.doc: The product of two sine transforms is even in its frequency.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.stieltjes_denominator_ne_zero
newHelpers.doc:
The Stieltjes denominator has no zeros on the slit plane for nonnegative integration
variables.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.stieltjesKernel_aestronglyMeasurable
newHelpers.doc: Convergence at a positive real point supplies measurability of all Stieltjes kernels.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.stieltjesKernel_locally_dominated
newHelpers.doc:
A local slit-plane denominator bound dominates the Stieltjes kernel by its integrable
norm at one positive real point.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integrable_stieltjesKernel
newHelpers.doc: Absolute convergence at one positive point implies convergence at every slit-plane point.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.iteratedDeriv_stieltjesKernel
newHelpers.doc: Repeated differentiation of the rational Stieltjes kernel.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integrable_abs_mul_exp_neg_abs
newHelpers.doc: The first absolute moment of a two-sided exponential is integrable.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.gaussian_normalization
newHelpers.doc: Converting the Gaussian integral constant to the principal DLMF normalization.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.eventually_norm_sector_iff
newHelpers.doc: Eventual assertions in a sector can be stated using one radial cutoff.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.ritt_derivative_bound
newHelpers.doc:
The Cauchy estimate has a constant independent of the size of the eventual power
bound, so the same estimate handles both big-O and little-o.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.laplace_derivatives_exp_bound
newHelpers.doc:
An exponential bound on one derivative supplies a common, slightly larger
exponential rate for all lower derivatives on the nonnegative half-line.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_eq_sum_add_remainder
newHelpers.doc:
Repeated integration by parts for the finite Fourier integral, with an exact
remainder involving the next one-sided derivative.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.norm_fourier_remainder_le
newHelpers.doc:
The modulus of the finite Fourier remainder is bounded by the integral of the
modulus of its highest derivative.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_boundary_limit
newHelpers.doc:
One integration by parts determines the limiting boundary phase from two
successive oscillatory integrals.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_boundary_tendsto_zero
newHelpers.doc: Convergence at two frequencies forces the boundary phase to tend to zero.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.fourier_Ioi_eq_sum_add_remainder
newHelpers.doc:
Repeated integration by parts for an improper Fourier integral, after its
boundary terms have been shown to vanish.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.tendsto_zero_of_uniform_fourier_Ioi
newHelpers.doc:
Uniform convergence on a frequency half-line transfers the finite-interval
Riemann–Lebesgue limit to the improper Fourier integral.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.harmonic_remainder_eq_integral
newHelpers.doc:
The harmonic remainder is a Binet integral, using the digamma value at a
positive integer and the same Bernoulli coefficients as in the Gamma expansion.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.invScale_isBigO_of_le
newHelpers.doc: Later inverse-power scales are bounded by earlier ones on the positive integers.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.sum_harmonicCoeff_even
newHelpers.doc:
Pairing consecutive Bernoulli coefficients recovers the customary harmonic
polynomial with only even powers after the first term.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.rpow_le_mul_on_unit_interval
newHelpers.doc:
On a positive unit interval starting at `a ≥ 1`, any real power is bounded
by its value at `a` times a constant depending only on the exponent.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.oscillatorySum_remainder_isBigO
newHelpers.doc: The sum of the Taylor errors of the power weight has the next-order power bound.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Gamma.hasSum_binetBeta_div_sub_binetPoly
newHelpers.doc:
The remainder of the Bernoulli expansion of Binet's kernel is an absolutely
convergent partial-fraction series with alternating sign.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Gamma.binetBeta_div_sub_binetPoly_sign
newHelpers.doc: The Bernoulli remainder of Binet's kernel has sign `(-1)^n` on the positive axis.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Gamma.digamma_sub_stirling_eq_integral
newHelpers.doc:
The remainder in the digamma expansion is the negative Laplace integral of
Binet's Bernoulli remainder; this identity holds at every positive real argument.

newHelpers.name: Asymptotics.norm_le_mul_exp_of_hasDerivWithinAt
newHelpers.doc:
An exponential bound for a continuous derivative on the nonnegative half-line
gives an explicit bound of the same positive exponential rate for the primitive.

newHelpers.name: Real.sum_Ico_rpow_le_one_add_integral
newHelpers.doc: A decreasing real power has partial sums bounded by one plus its integral.

newHelpers.name: Real.sum_Ico_rpow_isBigO_one
newHelpers.doc: Partial sums of a summable real power are bounded.

newHelpers.name: Real.sum_Ico_rpow_neg_one_isBigO_log
newHelpers.doc: The harmonic partial sums are bounded by a constant times the logarithm.

newHelpers.name: Real.sum_Ico_rpow_isBigO
newHelpers.doc: For exponent greater than `-1`, the partial power sum is `O(n^(p+1))`.

newHelpers.name: Real.sum_Ico_rpow_isBigO_add_one
newHelpers.doc: Away from exponent `-1`, a bound valid on both sides of the summability threshold.

newHelpers.name: Complex.exists_pos_forall_closedBall_arg_lt
newHelpers.doc:
A uniform relative disc around a point of a closed sector stays in a larger open
sector, and the norms in the disc remain comparable to the center norm.

newHelpers.name: Real.rpow_le_two_rpow_abs_mul
newHelpers.doc:
Real powers of two comparable positive numbers differ by at most a factor
`2 ^ |p|`, for positive and negative exponents alike.

newHelpers.name: Complex.exists_pos_forall_closedBall_rotated_arg_lt
newHelpers.doc: The uniform relative-disc estimate is invariant under rotation of the sector.

newHelpers.name: Complex.exists_pos_norm_deriv_le_of_sector_bound
newHelpers.doc:
Cauchy's derivative estimate transfers a power bound in an open sector to the next
power in an interior closed sector. The constant is independent of the function and the
radial cutoff, which also permits little-o applications.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_fourier_mul_eq_flip
newHelpers.doc: The bilinear Fourier pairing can be interchanged for two integrable functions.

newHelpers.name: Real.ae_fourier_eq_fourier_toLp
newHelpers.doc:
On `L¹ ∩ L²`, the Fourier integral agrees almost everywhere with the unitary
Fourier transform of the `L²` representative.

newHelpers.name: Real.memLp_fourier
newHelpers.doc: The Fourier integral of an integrable square-integrable function is square integrable.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_fourier_mul_conj_eq
newHelpers.doc: Parseval's pairing for classical Fourier integrals on `L¹ ∩ L²`.

newHelpers.name: intervalIntegral.integral_cexp_mul_eq_boundary_sub
newHelpers.doc: One integration by parts against `exp(z t)`, allowing one-sided endpoint derivatives.

newHelpers.name: intervalIntegral.integral_cexp_mul_eq_sum_add
newHelpers.doc:
Repeated integration by parts gives an exact finite boundary sum and remainder
for a complex exponential kernel and a sequence of successive derivatives.

newHelpers.name: Complex.eq_zero_of_tendsto_mul_exp_pi_I
newHelpers.doc:
If a function and its product with the phase `exp(π i t)` both have limits at
positive infinity, the first limit is zero. Even and odd integer subsequences
force the two candidate limits to be equal and opposite.

newHelpers.name: MeasureTheory.integral_eq_integral_Ioi_add_neg
newHelpers.doc: Splitting an integrable function into its positive and reflected negative halves.

newHelpers.name: MeasureTheory.MemLp.comp_abs
newHelpers.doc:
Even extension from the positive half-line preserves `Lᵖ` membership. The value
at zero is irrelevant for Lebesgue measure.

newHelpers.name: MeasureTheory.integral_comp_abs_eq_two_smul
newHelpers.doc:
The integral of an even extension is twice its positive-half integral, also
for totalized Bochner integrals when the integrability condition fails.

statementIssues.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.haar_isLittleO_pow
statementIssues.status: retained as admitted; suspected missing derivative compatibility
statementIssues.explanation: Holomorphy is assumed only for Q-F, whereas derivative data use iteratedDeriv j Q - iteratedDeriv j F. With Q z = conj z + z and F z = conj z, both separate totalized first derivatives vanish, but the derivative of Q-F is 1. This shows the missing compatibility, rather than a complete counterexample satisfying all Haar hypotheses. Individual holomorphy or explicit derivative compatibility would justify integration by parts.

retainedRedundantHypotheses: fourierCosTransform_gaussian: positivity of the frequency is not needed by the proof.
laplace_error_bound: nonvanishing of the highest derivative at zero is not needed by the proof.
